title: Nine Inches of Holding
subtitle: 筷子与餐具 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 筷子与餐具（历史社会与文化·饮食文化）
meta: 主题语境：筷子与餐具（历史社会与文化·饮食文化）　|　核心词汇：chopsticks　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chopsticks 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my mother was sent to hold ① chopsticks she could not use, and she said the holding was the whole of the lesson. The ② chopsticks, meaning the pair and not the meal, were nine inches long and were held by whoever came last; chopsticks, she said, are the only thing on a table that is judged by how much has been taken out of them.

Every ③ chopsticks on that table had the same grain, and the ④ chopsticks at the end, meaning the ones the host kept and not either of those, were the only ones anybody ever held properly. Chopsticks, my grandmother said, are nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chopsticks were the whole of the dinner, meaning the custom they carried and not the pair. The ⑥ chopsticks, meaning the custom and not any of that, are the only thing in a dinner that everybody shares and nobody questions; chopsticks, he said, are either something you hold or the only word that means both a pair and a custom. She said the custom is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ chopsticks had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the grain. The ⑧ chopsticks of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, were nine inches and eleven years of holding; chopsticks, she said, are either the ones at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chopsticks I remember are the ones at the end, which were held in 1973 and are still described as the straightest in the county. A ⑩ pair of chopsticks, my grandmother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being held; every pair of chopsticks, she said, is a custom that has agreed to look like a pair. She said the custom was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 筷子（指那一双筷子本身，与那顿饭相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold chopsticks 握筷子
D. n. 筷子（指那张桌上每一双）
E. n. 筷子（指末尾那一双）
F. n. 食俗（抽象：它承载的那个习俗）
G. n. 那个习俗（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chopsticks, meaning the pair and not the meal
chopsticks were the whole of the dinner
the chopsticks had become a number in a report
The chopsticks of the whole thing

answers.why: hold chopsticks 意为“握筷子”，1953 年母亲被派去握她使不惯的那双筷子。
chopsticks 意为“筷子”，指那一双筷子本身而不是那顿饭，长九英寸，由最后来的人握。
chopsticks 指那张桌上每一双筷子，每一双都是同样的纹理。
chopsticks 指末尾那一双（主人留下的那一双），是唯一有人认真握过的。
chopsticks 意为“食俗”，抽象指它承载的那个习俗，父亲说 chopsticks 就是那顿饭的全部。
chopsticks 为抽象用法，指那个习俗本身，是一顿饭里人人都共享、却没人质疑的东西。
chopsticks 意为“筷子”，到 1968 年这双 chopsticks 成了报告里的一个数字。
chopsticks 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸和十一年的握持。
chopsticks 意为“筷子”，我记得的是末尾那一双，1973 年握过，至今仍被说成全县最直的。
chopsticks 为抽象总称，祖母说一双筷子是唯一会因为被认真握持而变好的东西。
